- Salt identity and concentration: 1.0 M NaPF6：Table 1 lists 1.0 M NaPF6 for all four electrolyte groups G1-G4, matching the candidate's salt and concentration. [0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec11]
- Solvent system: EC/PC/DEC 25:25:50 by volume with 5% FEC：Table 1 gives 25% EC, 25% PC, 50% DEC and 5% FEC for the baseline electrolyte, exactly matching the candidate's solvent ratios and FEC content. [0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec11]
- Additive identity and amount: 3% adiponitrile (ADN)：Group G3 in Table 1 contains 3% ADN, and the text identifies 3% ADN as giving the most obvious improvement; this equals the candidate's 3% ADN. [0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec11][0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec8::child0]
- Improvement of initial Coulombic efficiency after formation：The sources report discharge capacities, rate retention, OCV/voltage plateaus, impedance and cycling stability, but never report or compare initial Coulombic efficiency (first-cycle charge/discharge ratio) for G3 or any group, so the specific target metric is not evidenced. 
- Operation at -20 C with improved low-temperature performance：The conclusion states the battery with 3% ADN shows a 13% discharge capacity increase at -20 C, directly supporting low-temperature benefit for this composition. [0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec8::child0]
- Formation step present before testing：Battery assembly describes a formation-like protocol: charge at 0.05 C for 180 min then 0.1 C for 360 min, followed by degassing and repackaging, establishing a formation context. [0061_Song 等 - 2018 - The effects of the functional electrolyte additive on the cathode material Na076Ni03Fe04Mn03O2 f::sec5::child0]
文献与候选的关联：Candidate c4-adn (1.0 M NaPF6, EC/PC/DEC 25/25/50 vol, 5% FEC, 3% ADN) is compositionally identical to electrolyte G3 in Song 2018, which was tested in a Na0.76Ni0.3Fe0.4Mn0.3O2 cathode / hard carbon anode pouch full cell; thus the reported -20 C and cycling results are associated with exactly this formulation. ## 文献依据与已记录的计算结果
- A baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving NaPF $_6$ (1 mol/L) into a mixed solvent of EC and EMC (weight ratio 3:7). To formulate a functional electrolyte, 1 wt% 2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA) was added to the baseline system. [0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec4::child0]
- A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . [0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec2::child0]
- Furthermore, pouch cells utilizing SA-based electrolytes displayed a significantly enhanced initial coulombic efficiency (Fig. 3h). [0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec7::child8]
- Under more extreme conditions, discharge tests at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Fig. 4a) revealed that cells with SA-based electrolyte delivered discharge capacities of 758.6, 702.2 and $638.2\mathrm{mAh}$ at $0.2\mathrm{C}$ , $0.5\mathrm{C}$ , and $1\mathrm{C}$ ( $1\mathrm{C} = 900\mathrm{mA}$ ), respectively, outperforming those with the baseline electrolyte, which exhibited 706.3, 636.8 and $563.6\mathrm{mAh}$ . [0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec7::child10]
- Fig. 4. (a) The low-temperature discharge performance at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and (b) the cycling performance at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ of pouch NFM/HC cells with different electrolytes. [0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec7::child11]
- The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . [0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec2::child0]
- In addition, high-voltage cycling (Fig. 4e) confirmed the excellent stability of the SA-containing electrolyte, with a marked improvement in capacity retention from $74.88\%$ to $86.32\%$ after 300 cycles at elevated cut-off voltages. [0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec7::child11]

## 下一步核查与验证
- 实验 1（核心缺口）：以 1 mol/L NaPF6 / EC:EMC = 3:7（质量比）为基准，对比 ±1 wt% SA 两组，在自建 硬碳||层状氧化物（NFM）软包全电池（N/P ≈ 1.1）上于 -20 °C 完成化成并报告首圈库仑效率数值；同时记录化成温度、化成倍率（建议 0.1 C）、截止电压（1.5–4.0 V）与首圈放电容量。
- 实验 2：将同一批电芯在 25 °C 化成后降至 -20 °C 放电，验证“化成条件”与“首效提升”的耦合：比较常温化成 vs -20 °C 化成的 ICE、首圈 dQ/dV 还原峰位置与阻抗。
- 实验 3：复用文献条件（-20 °C，0.2/0.5/1 C，1 C = 900 mA）复现 SA 与基准的放电容量差（758.6/702.2/638.2 mAh vs 706.3/636.8/563.6 mAh），确认电极/电解液批间一致性。
- 实验 4（机理归因）：用 XPS（F 1s、S 2p、C 1s）与 TOF-SIMS 比较 SA 与基准形成 SEI/CEI 的组成，并用 LSV/CV 标定 SA 的优先还原电位，验证首效提升来自 SA 优先成膜而非其他副反应。
- 验证 5（目标条件严格性）：文献只报告了 -20 °C 放电容量，而 ICE 的测试温度未注明；若项目以“-20 °C 化成后 ICE”为考核指标，需在上述测试中单独采集该项数据，本报告不将该指标写作已验证。
- 待补资料：文献未给出 SA 的价格对比或量产成本，成本目标仅有“由糖精合成、路线简便”的定性描述，需补充供应商报价与用量成本核算。
- 备选干预（本轮未获准入报告）：0.8 M NaPF6 / G2:MO = 7:3（CIE，仅在 -50 °C 半电池报告 HC 首效 80.5%）、1.0 wt% NaTFPB（软包首圈放电容量 1.35 Ah > 1.27 Ah）、3% ADN（-20 °C 放电容量 +13%）三者均缺少“硬碳||层状氧化物软包全电池在 -20 °C 化成后的首圈库仑效率”证据，可作为并行对照候选补充取证。

Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. A baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving NaPF $_6$ (1 mol/L) into a mixed solvent of EC and EMC (weight ratio 3:7). To formulate a functional electrolyte, 1 wt% 2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA) was added to the baseline system. The NFM cathode and hard carbon (HC) anode active materials were procured from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode slurry consisted of 94.5 wt% NFM, 1.8 wt% PVDF, 1 wt% carbon nanotubes (CNT), 2.5 wt% Super P, and 0.2 wt% maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP), and was cast onto aluminum foil. The HC anode was composed of 95 wt% HC,

![](images/8bfcb630e9de984c98fbfc69f2dd0cb440e9bd8293373fa0ec9806e9fb6d55de.jpg)  
Fig. 1. 2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA) is introduced as electrolyte additive to enhance the electrochemical performance of pouch SIBs.

1.5 wt% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2 wt% styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 wt% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd.) was employed as the separator. The areal mass loadings of the cathode and anode were 33.0 and 20.1 mg/cm $^{2}$ , respectively, with a negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio of 1.1 (based on theoretical capacity calculation).

The radial distribution function of (d) Baseline electrolyte and (e) SA electrolyte. (f) The LSV curves of different electrolytes. (g) Moisture content before and after 7 days of storage of different electrolytes. (h) The first cycle Coulombic efficiency of batteries with different electrolytes. (i) Exchange density of electrolytes at Tafel plot. To validate the water-scavenging capability of the additive, the electrolyte's moisture content was analyzed before and after storage (Fig. 3g). It was observed that the SA-containing electrolyte exhibited a noticeable decrease in moisture content following storage, supporting the maintenance of stable electrochemical reactions. This effect may contribute to improved electrochemical performance at elevated temperatures. Furthermore, pouch cells utilizing SA-based electrolytes displayed a significantly enhanced initial coulombic efficiency (Fig. 3h). These findings collectively confirm that SA-containing electrolytes promote favorable electrochemical behavior. In addition, Tafel measurements were performed on both electrolytes, revealing that the exchange current density of the electrode in the SA-based system exceeded that of the baseline (Fig. 3i), indicating accelerated the interface reaction kinetics. This enhancement is particularly beneficial under low-temperature operating conditions.

source_refs.raw_quote: Under more extreme conditions, discharge tests at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Fig. 4a) revealed that cells with SA-based electrolyte delivered discharge capacities of 758.6, 702.2 and $638.2\mathrm{mAh}$ at $0.2\mathrm{C}$ , $0.5\mathrm{C}$ , and $1\mathrm{C}$ ( $1\mathrm{C} = 900\mathrm{mA}$ ), respectively, outperforming those with the baseline electrolyte, which exhibited 706.3, 636.8 and $563.6\mathrm{mAh}$ . These results confirm that SA facilitates higher energy density and improved capacity retention at low temperatures, rendering it well-suited for emergency storage applications in cold environments. In addition, the rate capability of sodium-ion batteries at ambient temperature is critical for practical deployment. High-rate performance enables rapid charge/discharge cycles, a requirement for power-intensive applications such as electric vehicles and portable electronics [27a,28]. As shown in Fig. 4d, the SA containing system exhibited superior rate capacity, indicating enhanced commercial viability. Long-term cycling at 1C was also evaluated at room temperature (Figs. 4c and S7). During extended cycling, the baseline electrolyte showed faster polarization growth, whereas the SA-based system demonstrated superior capacity retention and enhanced coulombic efficiency. These characteristics contribute to reduced energy losses and extended battery lifespan, which are advantageous for grid-scale and commercial energy storage [29].

source_refs.raw_quote: A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.

source_refs.raw_quote: To evaluate the electrochemical performance of the electrolyte, Na $^{+}$ HC cells were assembled. The structural characteristics of HC are shown in Fig. S13, and for HC, the reversible capacity during the first cycle is critical for less sodium loss. As shown in Fig. 3a, CIE provides a specific capacity of 300.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ and an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% during the first cycle at 25°C, while CCE and WSE provide specific capacities of 299.6 and 300.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ and ICE of 87.7% and 91.4%, respectively. The three electrolytes deliver similar reversible capacities, while CIE has the highest ICE. The severe electrolyte decomposition creates a thick SEI and affects ICE $^{30,31}$ , which may explain the lower ICE of CCE. For CIE and WSE, the introduction of anions enables the construction of inorganic-rich SEI, and the appropriate number of anions in CIE consumes less Na $^{+}$ during film formation, thus guaranteeing a high ICE for HC in CIE. The rate performance of HC is shown in Figure S14, where CIE still provides a specific capacity of $195.0 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $2 \, A g^{-1}$ , while CCE and WSE maintain a specific capacity of 204.6 and $131.4 \, mAh g^{-1}$ , respectively. This phenomenon suggests that the ionic conductivity plays a crucial role in the rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ . The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE.

source_refs.raw_quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

source_refs.raw_quote: The MO solvent is added into linear ether G2 to precisely regulate the solvation structure and expand the electrolyte's low-temperature range via an entropy-driven effect. Experiments and simulations reveal that the $Na^{+}-G2$ chelating coordination structure can be well co-embedded in HC negative electrode, avoiding the sluggish traditional desolvation process and significantly improving ion diffusion at low temperatures. Meanwhile, the high sodium salt dissociation ability of G2 ensures good ionic conductivity in electrolyte. And the dipole interaction between solvents drives an appropriate number of anions into the solvation sheath, inducing the formation of a thin layer of inorganic-rich SEI. This multi-scale synergistic design enables highly reversible and high-rate sodium storage at low temperatures. Consequently, the CIE enables HC to deliver an initial Coulombic efficiency of 80.5% at $-50\ ^{\circ}C$ and a capacity retention of 93% after 200 cycles. Moreover, an Ah-level full cell retains 163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ at 25 ${}^{\circ}C$ and 107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ at $-50\ ^{\circ}C$ . This study demonstrates the significance of the solvent co-embedding mechanism in improving low-temperature ion storage and provides a strategy for designing electrolytes toward cold environments.

source_refs.raw_quote: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are viable contenders for large-scale energy storage systems owing to the plentiful supply of sodium resources. However, the poor stability of electrolyte/ electrode interface severely limits the cycle life of SIBs. Herein, sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB), a boron-centered fluorinated organic sodium salt, is used as a bifunctional additive in the Base electrolyte (NaPF $_6$ in EC/DMC/FEC) for NaNi $_{0.33}$ Fe $_{0.33}$ Mn $_{0.33}$ O $_2$ |hard carbon pouch cells. Theoretical simulations and experimental studies demonstrate that NaTFPB modulates the first solvation shell structure of Na $^+$ and undergoes preferential redox reactions at both electrodes simultaneously. This behaviour contributes to the formation of robust interfacial layers. As a result, uniform and stable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) and solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers, enriched with NaF and boron compounds, are formed. The Ah-scale pouch cell with NaTFPB exhibits a high capacity retention of 79 % after 500 cycles at 1 C rate under room temperature. Remarkably, under harsh operational stress combining elevated temperature (45 °C) and an upper high cutoff voltage of 4.1 V, the cell retains 96 % capacity retention over 250 cycles. Additionally, it exhibits excellent low-temperature discharge capability at $-20$ °C.

source_refs.raw_quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

ABSTRACT
A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. 2.1. Preparation of the batteries
Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. A baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving NaPF $_6$ (1 mol/L) into a mixed solvent of EC and EMC (weight ratio 3:7). To formulate a functional electrolyte, 1 wt% 2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA) was added to the baseline system. The NFM cathode and hard carbon (HC) anode active materials were procured from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode slurry consisted of 94.5 wt% NFM, 1.8 wt% PVDF, 1 wt% carbon nanotubes (CNT), 2.5 wt% Super P, and 0.2 wt% maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP), and was cast onto aluminum foil. The HC anode was composed of 95 wt% HC,

![](images/8bfcb630e9de984c98fbfc69f2dd0cb440e9bd8293373fa0ec9806e9fb6d55de.jpg)  
Fig. 1. 2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA) is introduced as electrolyte additive to enhance the electrochemical performance of pouch SIBs.

1.5 wt% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2 wt% styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 wt% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd.) was employed as the separator. The areal mass loadings of the cathode and anode were 33.0 and 20.1 mg/cm $^{2}$ , respectively, with a negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio of 1.1 (based on theoretical capacity calculation). The dry pouch cells were evacuated at 80 °C for 72 h, transferred into an argon-filled glovebox, and injected with 6.0 g of electrolyte. All other fabrication procedures followed standard practices in battery assembly.

These results confirm that SA facilitates higher energy density and improved capacity retention at low temperatures, rendering it well-suited for emergency storage applications in cold environments. In addition, the rate capability of sodium-ion batteries at ambient temperature is critical for practical deployment. High-rate performance enables rapid charge/discharge cycles, a requirement for power-intensive applications such as electric vehicles and portable electronics [27a,28]. As shown in Fig. 4d, the SA containing system exhibited superior rate capacity, indicating enhanced commercial viability. Long-term cycling at 1C was also evaluated at room temperature (Figs. 4c and S7). During extended cycling, the baseline electrolyte showed faster polarization growth, whereas the SA-based system demonstrated superior capacity retention and enhanced coulombic efficiency. These characteristics contribute to reduced energy losses and extended battery lifespan, which are advantageous for grid-scale and commercial energy storage [29].

association_citations.chunk_id: 0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec2
association_citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for development of all-climate carbonate electrolyte and it offers the straight approach to high-performance commercial pouch SIBs.

Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. The HC anode was composed of 95 wt% HC,

The slurry was spread on a copper foil (thickness 18 $\mu$ m) and dried at 80 °C for 8–12 h. citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

citations.quote: To evaluate the electrochemical performance of the electrolyte, Na $^{+}$ HC cells were assembled. The structural characteristics of HC are shown in Fig. S13, and for HC, the reversible capacity during the first cycle is critical for less sodium loss. As shown in Fig. 3a, CIE provides a specific capacity of 300.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ and an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% during the first cycle at 25°C, while CCE and WSE provide specific capacities of 299.6 and 300.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ and ICE of 87.7% and 91.4%, respectively. The three electrolytes deliver similar reversible capacities, while CIE has the highest ICE. The severe electrolyte decomposition creates a thick SEI and affects ICE $^{30,31}$ , which may explain the lower ICE of CCE. For CIE and WSE, the introduction of anions enables the construction of inorganic-rich SEI, and the appropriate number of anions in CIE consumes less Na $^{+}$ during film formation, thus guaranteeing a high ICE for HC in CIE. The rate performance of HC is shown in Figure S14, where CIE still provides a specific capacity of $195.0 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $2 \, A g^{-1}$ , while CCE and WSE maintain a specific capacity of 204.6 and $131.4 \, mAh g^{-1}$ , respectively. This phenomenon suggests that the ionic conductivity plays a crucial role in the rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ . The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE.

citations.quote: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are viable contenders for large-scale energy storage systems owing to the plentiful supply of sodium resources. However, the poor stability of electrolyte/ electrode interface severely limits the cycle life of SIBs. Herein, sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB), a boron-centered fluorinated organic sodium salt, is used as a bifunctional additive in the Base electrolyte (NaPF $_6$ in EC/DMC/FEC) for NaNi $_{0.33}$ Fe $_{0.33}$ Mn $_{0.33}$ O $_2$ |hard carbon pouch cells. Theoretical simulations and experimental studies demonstrate that NaTFPB modulates the first solvation shell structure of Na $^+$ and undergoes preferential redox reactions at both electrodes simultaneously. This behaviour contributes to the formation of robust interfacial layers. As a result, uniform and stable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) and solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers, enriched with NaF and boron compounds, are formed. The Ah-scale pouch cell with NaTFPB exhibits a high capacity retention of 79 % after 500 cycles at 1 C rate under room temperature. Remarkably, under harsh operational stress combining elevated temperature (45 °C) and an upper high cutoff voltage of 4.1 V, the cell retains 96 % capacity retention over 250 cycles. Additionally, it exhibits excellent low-temperature discharge capability at $-20$ °C.

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, adiponitrile (ADN) has a stronger ability of electron donating than the carbonate solvents and thus is easier to be reduced on the surface of the cathode material to form the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) film, so ADN is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time.

citations.quote: $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min.

citations.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

This effect may contribute to improved electrochemical performance at elevated temperatures. Furthermore, pouch cells utilizing SA-based electrolytes displayed a significantly enhanced initial coulombic efficiency (Fig. 3h). In addition, Tafel measurements were performed on both electrolytes, revealing that the exchange current density of the electrode in the SA-based system exceeded that of the baseline (Fig. 3i), indicating accelerated the interface reaction kinetics. This enhancement is particularly beneficial under low-temperature operating conditions.

These results confirm that SA facilitates higher energy density and improved capacity retention at low temperatures, rendering it well-suited for emergency storage applications in cold environments. In addition, the rate capability of sodium-ion batteries at ambient temperature is critical for practical deployment. High-rate performance enables rapid charge/discharge cycles, a requirement for power-intensive applications such as electric vehicles and portable electronics [27a,28]. As shown in Fig. 4d, the SA containing system exhibited superior rate capacity, indicating enhanced commercial viability. Long-term cycling at 1C was also evaluated at room temperature (Figs. 4c and S7). During extended cycling, the baseline electrolyte showed faster polarization growth, whereas the SA-based system demonstrated superior capacity retention and enhanced coulombic efficiency. These characteristics contribute to reduced energy losses and extended battery lifespan, which are advantageous for grid-scale and commercial energy storage [29].

evidence_ledger.quote: A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.

evidence_ledger.quote: The sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ , 99.8% min), diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G2, 99.8% min) and 2-methyloxolane (MO, 99.8% min) were purchased from DoDo Chem. Common ether electrolyte (CCE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2 solvent. Weakly solvated electrolyte (WSE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in MO solvent. Co-intercalated electrolyte (CIE) was prepared by dissolving 0.8 M NaPF $_6$ in G2: MO = 7:3 vol%. All electrolyte preparation processes were carried out in a glovebox filled with Ar (H $_2$ O < 0.1 ppm and O $_2$ < 0.1 ppm). The electrolyte salts and solvents we purchased are of anhydrous grade. After purchase, they are placed in the glove box for direct use. Hard carbon (HC) materials were purchased from Baisige New Energy Co., Ltd. The HC negative electrode was prepared by mixing the active material, CMC (CMC2200, purchased from Daicel Corporation), SBR (BM-451B, purchased from Zeon Corporation) and conductive carbon black (weight ratio 92:1.5:3.5:3) in deionized water to form a homogeneous slurry. The slurry was spread on a copper foil (thickness 18 $\mu$ m) and dried at 80 °C for 8–12 h. Then, it was perforated into a circular electrode sheet with a diameter of 12 mm and a loading of 2.5–3.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ . Glass fiber (GF/D, Whatman) was used as separator and metallic sodium (purchased from Canrd Technology Co. Ltd.) was used as counter electrode.

evidence_ledger.quote: To evaluate the electrochemical performance of the electrolyte, Na $^{+}$ HC cells were assembled. The structural characteristics of HC are shown in Fig. S13, and for HC, the reversible capacity during the first cycle is critical for less sodium loss. As shown in Fig. 3a, CIE provides a specific capacity of 300.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ and an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% during the first cycle at 25°C, while CCE and WSE provide specific capacities of 299.6 and 300.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ and ICE of 87.7% and 91.4%, respectively. The three electrolytes deliver similar reversible capacities, while CIE has the highest ICE. The severe electrolyte decomposition creates a thick SEI and affects ICE $^{30,31}$ , which may explain the lower ICE of CCE. For CIE and WSE, the introduction of anions enables the construction of inorganic-rich SEI, and the appropriate number of anions in CIE consumes less Na $^{+}$ during film formation, thus guaranteeing a high ICE for HC in CIE. The rate performance of HC is shown in Figure S14, where CIE still provides a specific capacity of $195.0 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $2 \, A g^{-1}$ , while CCE and WSE maintain a specific capacity of 204.6 and $131.4 \, mAh g^{-1}$ , respectively. This phenomenon suggests that the ionic conductivity plays a crucial role in the rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ . The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE.

evidence_ledger.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

evidence_ledger.quote: The MO solvent is added into linear ether G2 to precisely regulate the solvation structure and expand the electrolyte's low-temperature range via an entropy-driven effect. Experiments and simulations reveal that the $Na^{+}-G2$ chelating coordination structure can be well co-embedded in HC negative electrode, avoiding the sluggish traditional desolvation process and significantly improving ion diffusion at low temperatures. Meanwhile, the high sodium salt dissociation ability of G2 ensures good ionic conductivity in electrolyte. And the dipole interaction between solvents drives an appropriate number of anions into the solvation sheath, inducing the formation of a thin layer of inorganic-rich SEI. This multi-scale synergistic design enables highly reversible and high-rate sodium storage at low temperatures. Consequently, the CIE enables HC to deliver an initial Coulombic efficiency of 80.5% at $-50\ ^{\circ}C$ and a capacity retention of 93% after 200 cycles. Moreover, an Ah-level full cell retains 163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ at 25 ${}^{\circ}C$ and 107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ at $-50\ ^{\circ}C$ . This study demonstrates the significance of the solvent co-embedding mechanism in improving low-temperature ion storage and provides a strategy for designing electrolytes toward cold environments.

evidence_ledger.quote: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are viable contenders for large-scale energy storage systems owing to the plentiful supply of sodium resources. However, the poor stability of electrolyte/ electrode interface severely limits the cycle life of SIBs. Herein, sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB), a boron-centered fluorinated organic sodium salt, is used as a bifunctional additive in the Base electrolyte (NaPF $_6$ in EC/DMC/FEC) for NaNi $_{0.33}$ Fe $_{0.33}$ Mn $_{0.33}$ O $_2$ |hard carbon pouch cells. Theoretical simulations and experimental studies demonstrate that NaTFPB modulates the first solvation shell structure of Na $^+$ and undergoes preferential redox reactions at both electrodes simultaneously. This behaviour contributes to the formation of robust interfacial layers. As a result, uniform and stable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) and solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers, enriched with NaF and boron compounds, are formed. The Ah-scale pouch cell with NaTFPB exhibits a high capacity retention of 79 % after 500 cycles at 1 C rate under room temperature. Remarkably, under harsh operational stress combining elevated temperature (45 °C) and an upper high cutoff voltage of 4.1 V, the cell retains 96 % capacity retention over 250 cycles. Additionally, it exhibits excellent low-temperature discharge capability at $-20$ °C.

evidence_ledger.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

evidence_ledger.quote:
ABSTRACT
A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for development of all-climate carbonate electrolyte and it offers the straight approach to high-performance commercial pouch SIBs.

Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for development of all-climate carbonate electrolyte and it offers the straight approach to high-performance commercial pouch SIBs.

ABSTRACT
A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for development of all-climate carbonate electrolyte and it offers the straight approach to high-performance commercial pouch SIBs.

citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

citations.quote: The influence of incorporating various concentrations of NaTFPB on the NFM111 cathode was investigated through electrochemical measurements employing NFM111||Na half-cells. The rate capabilities of the half-cells with different electrolytes are depicted in Fig. 2a. Notably, the electrolyte containing 1.0 wt% NaTFPB exhibits superior rate performance, especially at high currents, due to its low interfacial resistance compared to the electrolytes with other concentrations. citations.quote: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are viable contenders for large-scale energy storage systems owing to the plentiful supply of sodium resources. However, the poor stability of electrolyte/ electrode interface severely limits the cycle life of SIBs. Herein, sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB), a boron-centered fluorinated organic sodium salt, is used as a bifunctional additive in the Base electrolyte (NaPF $_6$ in EC/DMC/FEC) for NaNi $_{0.33}$ Fe $_{0.33}$ Mn $_{0.33}$ O $_2$ |hard carbon pouch cells. Theoretical simulations and experimental studies demonstrate that NaTFPB modulates the first solvation shell structure of Na $^+$ and undergoes preferential redox reactions at both electrodes simultaneously. This behaviour contributes to the formation of robust interfacial layers. As a result, uniform and stable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) and solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers, enriched with NaF and boron compounds, are formed. The Ah-scale pouch cell with NaTFPB exhibits a high capacity retention of 79 % after 500 cycles at 1 C rate under room temperature. Remarkably, under harsh operational stress combining elevated temperature (45 °C) and an upper high cutoff voltage of 4.1 V, the cell retains 96 % capacity retention over 250 cycles. Additionally, it exhibits excellent low-temperature discharge capability at $-20$ °C.

The cell containing the NaTFPB additive maintains a high capacity retention of 79 % after 500 cycles at a current density of 1.0 C, whereas the cell with the Base electrolyte retains only 62 % of its capacity. The rapid capacity degradation of the Base electrolyte cell is attributed to the poor stability of CEI/SEI and continuous decomposition of the electrolyte. The digital photographs of cycled electrodes reveal that the Base system exhibits yellow and white decomposition products while the electrodes with NaTFPB appear clean (Fig. S19). After 500 cycles, the discharge capacity of the Base electrolyte system drops to 0.79 Ah, while the NaTFPB system still maintains an impressive capacity of 1.07 Ah. It is worth emphasizing that the pouch cell with the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibits significant advantages in cycling performance compared to those of the previous research findings (Fig. S20).

citations.quote: It is worth emphasizing that the pouch cell with the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibits significant advantages in cycling performance compared to those of the previous research findings (Fig. S20). Moreover, the NaTFPB additive also significantly enhances the cycling stability of pouch cells under high temperature and high voltage conditions (Fig. 7d). Under harsh conditions of 4.1 V and 45 °C, the pouch cell with Base electrolyte experienced a sharp capacity retention drop to 80 % after only 112 cycles (Fig. S21). This is attributed to the continuous decomposition of organic solvents, leading to severe gas generation within the pouch cell. In contrast, the NaTFPB additive stabilizes the interface by forming robust SEI/CEI layers enriched with NaF and boron compounds, significantly suppressing gas generation (Fig. S22). As a result, the pouch cell with NaTFPB maintained an exceptional capacity retention of 96 % after 250 cycles. When the working temperature decreases to -20 °C, the pouch cell with NaTFBP additive displays discharge capacities of 1.07 Ah at 0.5 C under a high voltage of 4.1 V (Fig. 7e), much higher than that with the Base electrolyte (1.01 Ah).

Xiaona Song $^{a,b}$ , Tao Meng $^{a}$ , Yaoming Deng $^{a,b}$ , Aimei Gao $^{a}$ , Junmin Nan $^{a}$ , Dong

Shu $^{a,c,d,*}$ , Fenyun Yi $^{a}$

$^{a}$ School of Chemistry and Environment, South China Normal University, Guangzhou 510006, PR China

$^{b}$ R&D centre, Dongguan McNair New Power Co., Ltd, Dongguan, Guangdong 523000, PR China

$^{d}$ Guangzhou Key Laboratory of Materials for Energy Conversion and Storage, Guangzhou 510006, PR China

\* Corresponding author E-mail address: dshu@scnu.edu.cn (Dong Shu)

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, adiponitrile (ADN) has a stronger ability of electron donating than the carbonate solvents and thus is easier to be reduced on the surface of the cathode material to form the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) film, so ADN is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time.

citations.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

validation_plan: 实验 1（核心缺口）：以 1 mol/L NaPF6 / EC:EMC = 3:7（质量比）为基准，对比 ±1 wt% SA 两组，在自建 硬碳||层状氧化物（NFM）软包全电池（N/P ≈ 1.1）上于 -20 °C 完成化成并报告首圈库仑效率数值；同时记录化成温度、化成倍率（建议 0.1 C）、截止电压（1.5–4.0 V）与首圈放电容量。
实验 2：将同一批电芯在 25 °C 化成后降至 -20 °C 放电，验证“化成条件”与“首效提升”的耦合：比较常温化成 vs -20 °C 化成的 ICE、首圈 dQ/dV 还原峰位置与阻抗。
实验 3：复用文献条件（-20 °C，0.2/0.5/1 C，1 C = 900 mA）复现 SA 与基准的放电容量差（758.6/702.2/638.2 mAh vs 706.3/636.8/563.6 mAh），确认电极/电解液批间一致性。
实验 4（机理归因）：用 XPS（F 1s、S 2p、C 1s）与 TOF-SIMS 比较 SA 与基准形成 SEI/CEI 的组成，并用 LSV/CV 标定 SA 的优先还原电位，验证首效提升来自 SA 优先成膜而非其他副反应。
验证 5（目标条件严格性）：文献只报告了 -20 °C 放电容量，而 ICE 的测试温度未注明；若项目以“-20 °C 化成后 ICE”为考核指标，需在上述测试中单独采集该项数据，本报告不将该指标写作已验证。
待补资料：文献未给出 SA 的价格对比或量产成本，成本目标仅有“由糖精合成、路线简便”的定性描述，需补充供应商报价与用量成本核算。
备选干预（本轮未获准入报告）：0.8 M NaPF6 / G2:MO = 7:3（CIE，仅在 -50 °C 半电池报告 HC 首效 80.5%）、1.0 wt% NaTFPB（软包首圈放电容量 1.35 Ah > 1.27 Ah）、3% ADN（-20 °C 放电容量 +13%）三者均缺少“硬碳||层状氧化物软包全电池在 -20 °C 化成后的首圈库仑效率”证据，可作为并行对照候选补充取证。

citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for development of all-climate carbonate electrolyte and it offers the straight approach to high-performance commercial pouch SIBs.

association_citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for development of all-climate carbonate electrolyte and it offers the straight approach to high-performance commercial pouch SIBs.

citations.quote: To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments.

citations.quote: To evaluate the electrochemical performance of the electrolyte, Na $^{+}$ HC cells were assembled. The structural characteristics of HC are shown in Fig. S13, and for HC, the reversible capacity during the first cycle is critical for less sodium loss. As shown in Fig. 3a, CIE provides a specific capacity of 300.5 mAh g $^{-1}$ and an initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 93.7% during the first cycle at 25°C, while CCE and WSE provide specific capacities of 299.6 and 300.1 mAh g $^{-1}$ and ICE of 87.7% and 91.4%, respectively. The three electrolytes deliver similar reversible capacities, while CIE has the highest ICE. The severe electrolyte decomposition creates a thick SEI and affects ICE $^{30,31}$ , which may explain the lower ICE of CCE. For CIE and WSE, the introduction of anions enables the construction of inorganic-rich SEI, and the appropriate number of anions in CIE consumes less Na $^{+}$ during film formation, thus guaranteeing a high ICE for HC in CIE. The rate performance of HC is shown in Figure S14, where CIE still provides a specific capacity of $195.0 \, mAh g^{-1}$ at $2 \, A g^{-1}$ , while CCE and WSE maintain a specific capacity of 204.6 and $131.4 \, mAh g^{-1}$ , respectively. This phenomenon suggests that the ionic conductivity plays a crucial role in the rate performance at $25^{\circ}C$ . The CIE effectively improves the ionic conductivity while retaining the co-intercalation behavior, so the rate performance is close to that of CCE.

citations.chunk_id: 0024_Hu 等 - 2025 - Bifunctional sodium tetrakis 35-bistrifluoromethylphenyl borate additive for long-lifespan sodi::sec3::child0
citations.quote: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are viable contenders for large-scale energy storage systems owing to the plentiful supply of sodium resources. However, the poor stability of electrolyte/ electrode interface severely limits the cycle life of SIBs. Herein, sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB), a boron-centered fluorinated organic sodium salt, is used as a bifunctional additive in the Base electrolyte (NaPF $_6$ in EC/DMC/FEC) for NaNi $_{0.33}$ Fe $_{0.33}$ Mn $_{0.33}$ O $_2$ |hard carbon pouch cells. Theoretical simulations and experimental studies demonstrate that NaTFPB modulates the first solvation shell structure of Na $^+$ and undergoes preferential redox reactions at both electrodes simultaneously. This behaviour contributes to the formation of robust interfacial layers. As a result, uniform and stable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) and solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers, enriched with NaF and boron compounds, are formed. The Ah-scale pouch cell with NaTFPB exhibits a high capacity retention of 79 % after 500 cycles at 1 C rate under room temperature. Remarkably, under harsh operational stress combining elevated temperature (45 °C) and an upper high cutoff voltage of 4.1 V, the cell retains 96 % capacity retention over 250 cycles. Additionally, it exhibits excellent low-temperature discharge capability at $-20$ °C.

Under harsh conditions of 4.1 V and 45 °C, the pouch cell with Base electrolyte experienced a sharp capacity retention drop to 80 % after only 112 cycles (Fig. S21). This is attributed to the continuous decomposition of organic solvents, leading to severe gas generation within the pouch cell. Xiaona Song $^{a,b}$ , Tao Meng $^{a}$ , Yaoming Deng $^{a,b}$ , Aimei Gao $^{a}$ , Junmin Nan $^{a}$ , Dong

Shu $^{a,c,d,*}$ , Fenyun Yi $^{a}$

\* Corresponding author E-mail address: dshu@scnu.edu.cn (Dong Shu)

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, adiponitrile (ADN) has a stronger ability of electron donating than the carbonate solvents and thus is easier to be reduced on the surface of the cathode material to form the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) film, so ADN is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time.

citations.quote: $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min.

citations.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

citations.quote: $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min.

## 配方筛选结果
获得文献支持的候选：c1-sa。

### 候选资料：c1-sa（通过筛选）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（质量）：EC=0.3, EMC=0.7；添加剂：2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride；添加剂用量：2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride=1 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec4::child0]：Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. A baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving NaPF $_6$ (1 mol/L) into a mixed solvent of EC and EMC (weight ratio 3:7). To formulate a functional electrolyte, 1 wt% 2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA) was added to the baseline system. The NFM cathode and hard carbon (HC) anode active materials were procured from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode slurry consisted of 94.5 wt% NFM, 1.8 wt% PVDF, 1 wt% carbon nanotubes (CNT), 2.5 wt% Super P, and 0.2 wt% maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP), and was cast onto aluminum foil. The HC anode was composed of 95 wt% HC,

![](images/8bfcb630e9de984c98fbfc69f2dd0cb440e9bd8293373fa0ec9806e9fb6d55de.jpg)  
Fig. 1. 2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA) is introduced as electrolyte additive to enhance the electrochemical performance of pouch SIBs.

1.5 wt% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2 wt% styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 wt% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd.) was employed as the separator. The areal mass loadings of the cathode and anode were 33.0 and 20.1 mg/cm $^{2}$ , respectively, with a negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio of 1.1 (based on theoretical capacity calculation).

## 候选评估

## 下一步核查与验证
- 实验 1（核心缺口）：以 1 mol/L NaPF6 / EC:EMC = 3:7（质量比）为基准，对比 ±1 wt% SA 两组，在自建 硬碳||层状氧化物（NFM）软包全电池（N/P ≈ 1.1）上于 -20 °C 完成化成并报告首圈库仑效率数值；同时记录化成温度、化成倍率（建议 0.1 C）、截止电压（1.5–4.0 V）与首圈放电容量。
- 实验 2：将同一批电芯在 25 °C 化成后降至 -20 °C 放电，验证“化成条件”与“首效提升”的耦合：比较常温化成 vs -20 °C 化成的 ICE、首圈 dQ/dV 还原峰位置与阻抗。
- 实验 3：复用文献条件（-20 °C，0.2/0.5/1 C，1 C = 900 mA）复现 SA 与基准的放电容量差（758.6/702.2/638.2 mAh vs 706.3/636.8/563.6 mAh），确认电极/电解液批间一致性。
- 实验 4（机理归因）：用 XPS（F 1s、S 2p、C 1s）与 TOF-SIMS 比较 SA 与基准形成 SEI/CEI 的组成，并用 LSV/CV 标定 SA 的优先还原电位，验证首效提升来自 SA 优先成膜而非其他副反应。
- 验证 5（目标条件严格性）：文献只报告了 -20 °C 放电容量，而 ICE 的测试温度未注明；若项目以“-20 °C 化成后 ICE”为考核指标，需在上述测试中单独采集该项数据，本报告不将该指标写作已验证。
- 待补资料：文献未给出 SA 的价格对比或量产成本，成本目标仅有“由糖精合成、路线简便”的定性描述，需补充供应商报价与用量成本核算。
- 备选干预（本轮未获准入报告）：0.8 M NaPF6 / G2:MO = 7:3（CIE，仅在 -50 °C 半电池报告 HC 首效 80.5%）、1.0 wt% NaTFPB（软包首圈放电容量 1.35 Ah > 1.27 Ah）、3% ADN（-20 °C 放电容量 +13%）三者均缺少“硬碳||层状氧化物软包全电池在 -20 °C 化成后的首圈库仑效率”证据，可作为并行对照候选补充取证。
